guides.title: How to Hire a Household Employee in Florida (2026 Guide)
guides.desc: Nanny tax, minimum wage, Florida reemployment tax and the paperwork families need when they hire a nanny, housekeeper or cook in Florida.
guides.html:
1. Is the worker your employee?

If you control what work is done and how it's done, the worker is generally your household employee — a nanny or housekeeper on your schedule, for example. If the worker runs their own business, brings their own tools and offers services to the public, they're generally self-employed (IRS Publication 926).

2. Pay at least minimum wage

The Florida minimum wage is $15.00/hour since September 30, 2026, and will be adjusted for inflation every year from 2027.

3. Federal taxes (the "nanny tax")

  • Social Security and Medicare: if you pay one household employee $3,000 or more in cash wages in 2026, you withhold 6.2% + 1.45% from their pay and pay the same amount yourself.
  • FUTA: if you pay $1,000 or more to household employees in any calendar quarter, you owe federal unemployment tax (6% on the first $7,000 per employee, usually reduced by state credit).
  • You report these on Schedule H with your Form 1040 and give the employee a Form W-2.
  • Wages paid to workers under 18 don't count for Social Security and Medicare unless household work is their main occupation.

4. Florida taxes

  • No state income tax to withhold.
  • Florida reemployment tax: applies if you pay $1,000 or more in a calendar quarter for domestic services; it's charged on the first $7,000 per employee per year, at 2.7% for new employers (Florida Department of Revenue).

5. Put it in writing

Agree in writing on hours, duties, pay, overtime, paid time off and how either side ends the arrangement.

Sources: IRS Publication 926 (2026) · Florida Department of Revenue — reemployment tax · Florida Constitution, Art. X §24.
faq: What is the nanny tax threshold for 2026?
$3,000 in cash wages paid to one household employee in the year (IRS Publication 926).
Do I need to withhold Florida income tax?
No. Florida has no state income tax.
guides.answer: To hire a household employee in Florida in 2026: pay at least the $15.00/hour state minimum wage; if you pay one worker $3,000 or more in the year, withhold and match Social Security and Medicare (7.65% each) and file Schedule H; pay Florida reemployment tax if wages reach $1,000 in a quarter. Florida has no state income tax.

guides.title: Nanny vs Babysitter: What's the Difference? (Orlando, FL)
guides.desc: The difference between a nanny and a babysitter: role, schedule, pay in Orlando and what changes for taxes when you hire one.
guides.answer: A nanny cares for your children on a regular schedule, often full-time, and takes part in their daily routine. A babysitter covers occasional hours, like date nights. In the Orlando metro area, childcare workers earn a median $15.00 an hour (BLS, May 2025), and Florida's minimum wage is $15.00.
guides.html:
The short version

NannyBabysitter
ScheduleRegular, set by the family: part-time or full-time, every weekOccasional: evenings, weekends, a few hours here and there
RolePart of the kids' daily routine: meals, naps, school runs, activities, homeworkKeeps the kids safe and happy while the parents are out
How you payUsually hourly or a weekly salary, paid every week or twoUsually hourly, paid at the end of each visit
TaxesOften a household employee once pay passes the yearly thresholdSame rule: it depends on how much you pay in the year, not on the title

What a nanny does

A nanny works on your schedule, often 20 to 50 hours a week, and becomes part of the family's routine. Typical duties: getting the kids ready, preparing their meals, school drop-off and pick-up, naps, activities, homework and the kids' laundry. Some families share one nanny between two households (a nanny share). Because the nanny works regular hours under your direction, she is usually your household employee.

What a babysitter does

A babysitter comes when you need her: a date night, a Saturday afternoon, an evening event. The job is to keep the kids safe, fed and entertained and to follow the bedtime routine. Many babysitters are students or nannies picking up extra hours.

Pay in Orlando

MeasureValueSource
Childcare workers, Orlando-Kissimmee-Sanford metro area, median wage$15.00/hr (mean $15.81)BLS OEWS, May 2025
Florida minimum wage$15.00/hour since September 30, 2026Florida Constitution, Art. X §24

The BLS figure covers childcare workers in all settings, including daycare centers, so it is a floor more than a target. Nannies with experience, CPR training, a car or a second language usually earn more, and so do babysitters on late nights and holidays. For more detail see how much a nanny costs in Orlando and how much to pay a babysitter.

Which one do you need?

  • You work and need care every weekday: a nanny.
  • You need a few hours now and then: a babysitter.
  • Your kids are in school and you need 3 to 4 hours every afternoon: a part-time nanny (sometimes called an after-school nanny).

Taxes

The IRS doesn't look at the job title. In 2026, if you pay any one household worker $3,000 or more in cash wages during the year, you owe Social Security and Medicare taxes on those wages (IRS Publication 926). That often applies to a nanny and sometimes to a regular babysitter. See nanny taxes in Florida.

faq: Is a nanny more expensive than a babysitter?
Not always per hour, but a nanny works many more hours, so the monthly cost is much higher. Experienced nannies and babysitters working late nights or holidays usually charge more.
Is a babysitter a household employee?
It depends on how much you pay. In 2026, if you pay one babysitter $3,000 or more in cash wages in the year, Social Security and Medicare taxes apply (IRS Publication 926).
Do I have to pay a nanny at least minimum wage in Florida?
If the nanny is your employee, yes. Florida's minimum wage is $15.00/hour since September 30, 2026.

guides.title: Do I Have to Pay Taxes for My Nanny or Housekeeper in Florida? (2026)
guides.desc: The 2026 household employer ("nanny tax") rules for Florida families: Social Security and Medicare, federal unemployment tax, Schedule H, W-2 and Florida reemployment tax.
guides.answer: Yes, if you pay one household worker $3,000 or more in cash wages in 2026: you owe Social Security and Medicare (7.65% from you, 7.65% withheld from them). Paying $1,000 or more in any quarter adds federal unemployment tax and Florida reemployment tax. Florida has no state income tax. You report federal taxes on Schedule H.
guides.html:
A nanny, housekeeper or private cook who works in your home, on your schedule and under your direction, is usually your household employee. That makes you a household employer. This is what the IRS and Florida expect from you in 2026.

1. Social Security and Medicare

  • Threshold: $3,000 or more in cash wages paid to one household employee in 2026.
  • Rates: Social Security 6.2% plus Medicare 1.45%, from the employee and the same from you: 7.65% each side.
  • Who doesn't count: wages paid to your spouse, to your child under 21, to your parent (with narrow exceptions), and to an employee under 18 at any time in 2026 unless household work is their main occupation.

2. Federal unemployment tax (FUTA)

  • Threshold: total cash wages of $1,000 or more to household employees in any calendar quarter of 2025 or 2026.
  • Rate: 6.0% of the first $7,000 you pay each employee in the year. You may get a credit of up to 5.4% for state unemployment tax, for a net rate of 0.6%. FUTA is paid only by you, never withheld from the employee.

3. Federal income tax

You don't have to withhold federal income tax. You withhold it only if your employee asks and you agree.

4. Paperwork and deadlines

  • Get an employer identification number (EIN) from the IRS; your Social Security number won't do.
  • You and your employee each complete Form I-9 (employment eligibility). Keep it; don't send it.
  • File Form W-2 for 2026 with the Social Security Administration by February 1, 2027, and give your employee a copy.
  • File Schedule H (Form 1040) with your 2026 federal return by April 15, 2027. To avoid a large bill, you can have more tax withheld from your own paycheck or make estimated payments during the year.

5. Florida

  • No state income tax. Florida has no personal income tax, so there's nothing to withhold for the state.
  • Reemployment tax (Florida's unemployment tax): a private home becomes liable after paying $1,000 in cash wages for domestic services in a calendar quarter. It applies to the first $7,000 of each employee's wages in the year, and the initial rate for new employers is 2.7%. Register with the Florida Department of Revenue. Employers of domestic employees only can file an annual report (Form RT-7) instead of quarterly ones.
  • Minimum wage: an employee must be paid at least the Florida minimum wage, $15.00/hour since September 30, 2026.

When the worker isn't your employee

If an agency provides the worker and controls what work is done and how, the worker isn't your employee. A house cleaner with her own business who cleans many homes, brings her own supplies and sets her own methods is often self-employed. Famyle is not an agency: when you hire through Famyle, the professional works for you.

Many families use a household payroll service or an accountant to handle this. See also how to hire a household employee in Florida and the housekeeper hiring checklist.

This is general information, not tax advice. Rules change every year; check IRS Publication 926 and the Florida Department of Revenue, or talk to a tax professional, for your situation.

  • Florida Department of Commerce: required notices (Florida minimum wage)
faq: What is the nanny tax threshold for 2026?
$3,000 in cash wages paid to one household employee during 2026. At that point Social Security and Medicare taxes apply to all of that employee's cash wages (IRS Publication 926).
Does Florida have a state income tax on nanny wages?
No. Florida has no personal income tax. Florida does have a reemployment tax for household employers who pay $1,000 or more in cash wages in a calendar quarter.
Do I need to give my nanny a W-2?
If you owe Social Security and Medicare taxes on their wages, yes. For 2026 wages, file the W-2 with the Social Security Administration by February 1, 2027.
Is my house cleaner my employee?
It depends on control. A housekeeper on your schedule is usually your employee; a cleaner who runs her own business, serves many clients and brings her own supplies is often self-employed.

guides.title: How to Hire a Housekeeper or House Cleaner in Orlando: Checklist
guides.desc: A practical checklist for hiring a housekeeper or house cleaner in Orlando, FL: tasks, hours, pay, trial day, references, written agreement, supplies and insurance.
guides.answer: To hire a housekeeper in Orlando: list the tasks, set days and hours, offer pay at or above the Florida minimum wage ($15.00/hour), call references, pay a trial day, put the agreement in writing, decide who buys supplies, and check your insurance. On Famyle you post the job free and hire directly.
guides.html:
Before you post

  1. List the tasks. Kitchen and bathrooms, floors, dusting, laundry, ironing, changing beds, organizing, inside the fridge or oven, windows. Say which rooms and which tasks are weekly versus occasional.
  2. Choose the type of help. A house cleaner usually comes for a few hours every week or two. A housekeeper works more regular hours and may also do laundry, organizing and errands.
  3. Set days and hours. Fixed days help both sides. Be realistic: a large home in Windermere or Horizon West takes longer than an apartment.
  4. Set the pay. In the Orlando metro area, maids and housekeeping cleaners earn a median $16.90 an hour (mean $17.84; BLS, May 2025). If she's your employee, pay at least the Florida minimum wage, $15.00/hour since September 30, 2026. Experience, a car, references and a larger home justify more. See house cleaning cost in Orlando.

Choosing the person

  1. Post your job on Famyle. Post it for free with the tasks, hours, area and pay. Local professionals apply and you talk to them directly.
  2. Interview. Ask about homes like yours (size, pets, kids), which tasks they do and don't do, availability, transportation and preferred products.
  3. Call references. Ask at least two families: how long she worked there, reliability, care with belongings, and why it ended. Famyle doesn't have reviews in the U.S. yet, so references are your best signal.
  4. Do a paid trial day. Pay for the trial at the agreed rate. Walk through the house together at the start and at the end.
  5. Decide about a background check. If you want one, you need the candidate's written permission. See background checks in Florida. Famyle does not run background checks.

Putting it in writing

  1. Written agreement. Days and hours, tasks, hourly rate or flat rate, how and when you pay, overtime, paid holidays or time off, what happens if either side cancels, notice to end the arrangement, and house rules (keys, alarm code, pets, privacy).
  2. Supplies. Agree on who buys products and equipment. If you supply them, keep them stocked; if she brings her own, agree on whether that's in the rate.
  3. Insurance. Ask your homeowner's insurance agent whether your policy covers injuries to someone working in your home, or whether you need more coverage. If she runs her own cleaning business, ask whether she carries her own insurance.
  4. Taxes. A housekeeper on your schedule is usually your household employee. In 2026, paying her $3,000 or more in cash wages in the year means Social Security and Medicare taxes. Read household employer taxes in Florida.

After the first month

Sit down for 10 minutes, review what's working and adjust the task list. Clear expectations are the main reason good housekeepers stay.

Find a housekeeper in Orlando Find a house cleaner

faq: How much should I pay a housekeeper in Orlando?
Maids and housekeeping cleaners in the Orlando metro area earn a median $16.90 an hour (BLS, May 2025). An employee must earn at least the Florida minimum wage, $15.00/hour since September 30, 2026.
Should I pay for a trial day?
Yes. Pay the trial at the agreed rate. It's fair to the professional and shows you how she works in your home.
Who buys the cleaning supplies?
Either side can; just agree upfront. If the cleaner brings her own products and equipment, that is usually reflected in the rate.
Is a housekeeper the same as a house cleaner?
Not quite. A house cleaner usually comes for a few hours every week or two; a housekeeper works more regular hours and may also handle laundry, organizing and errands.

guides.title: Background Checks for a Nanny in Florida: What's Allowed?
guides.desc: What Florida families can check before hiring a nanny: references, Florida's public sex offender registry, and background check reports under the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA).
guides.answer: Yes, you can check a nanny's background in Florida. You can call references and search Florida's public sex offender registry yourself. To buy a background report from a screening company, federal law (FCRA) requires a standalone written notice and the nanny's written permission, plus specific notices if you decide not to hire.
guides.html:
Famyle does not run background checks today. When you hire through Famyle, you decide what to check, and the steps below are yours to take.

What you can do yourself, for free

  • References. Call at least two families the nanny worked for. Ask how long, the ages of the kids, reliability, how she handled an emergency, and whether they would hire her again.
  • Florida sex offender registry. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) runs a public search of registered sexual offenders and predators, by name or near an address: offender.fdle.state.fl.us.
  • National sex offender search. The U.S. Department of Justice's National Sex Offender Public Website searches state registries together, useful if the nanny lived in other states.
  • Interview and trial day. Ask scenario questions (a fever, a fall, a stranger at the door) and do a paid trial day while you're home.

FDLE also offers a paid, name-based search of Florida criminal history records. It covers Florida records only.

If you use a background check company: the FCRA

When you buy a background report from a company that compiles them (a consumer reporting agency) to decide whether to hire someone, the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act applies. According to the FTC:

  1. Written notice, on its own. Tell the candidate in writing that you may use the report. The notice must be a stand-alone document, not part of an application.
  2. Written permission. Get the candidate's written permission before the check.
  3. Certify to the company that you gave notice, got permission and will follow the law.
  4. Before deciding not to hire because of the report, give the candidate a copy of the report and "A Summary of Your Rights Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act," so she can explain or correct errors.
  5. After deciding not to hire, tell her that the decision was based on the report; give the name, address and phone number of the company that sold it; say that the company didn't make the decision; and tell her she can dispute the report's accuracy.

Fair practices

  • Treat every candidate the same way: if you check one, check all finalists.
  • Be careful with what you learn: an old arrest without a conviction tells you little. Federal and state anti-discrimination laws may also apply to how you use background information.
  • Keep reports private and store them securely.

On Famyle

Families post a job for free, talk to the professionals who apply and hire directly. Because Famyle doesn't check backgrounds and doesn't have reviews in the U.S. yet, use references, the registry search and, if you want, a screening company with the steps above. See how Famyle works and nanny vs babysitter.

This is general information, not legal advice. For your situation, talk to an employment lawyer.

Find a nanny in Orlando

Sources

  • FTC: Background Checks: What Employers Need to Know
  • FDLE: Florida Sexual Offenders and Predators search
  • U.S. Department of Justice: National Sex Offender Public Website
  • FDLE: Florida Criminal History Record Check
faq: Can I run a background check on a nanny in Florida?

Yes. If you buy a report from a background check company, the federal FCRA requires a stand-alone written notice and the nanny's written permission first, and specific notices if you decide not to hire because of the report.
Is Florida's sex offender registry public?
Yes. FDLE offers a public online search of registered sexual offenders and predators by name or near an address at offender.fdle.state.fl.us.
Does Famyle do background checks on nannies?
Not today. Families decide what to check: references, the public registry search and, with written permission, a report from a screening company.
Do I need permission to call a nanny's references?
References are people the candidate gave you to call, so asking them is expected. The FCRA steps apply when you buy a report from a background check company.

guides_pt.title: Como contratar babá em Orlando: guia para famílias brasileiras (2026)
guides_pt.desc: Passo a passo para contratar babá ou nanny em Orlando: onde achar, quanto pagar, o que perguntar na entrevista e o que a lei da Flórida exige.
guides_pt.html:
Mudou para Orlando ou está chegando e precisa de alguém de confiança para cuidar das crianças? Este guia junta o que as famílias brasileiras mais perguntam: babá ou nanny, quanto custa, como escolher e o que muda em relação ao Brasil.

Babá, babysitter ou nanny?

  • Babysitter: cuida das crianças por algumas horas, à noite ou no fim de semana. Paga-se por hora.
  • Nanny: trabalha com rotina fixa, muitas vezes em tempo integral, e às vezes leva e busca na escola. É o mais parecido com a babá mensalista do Brasil.

Passo a passo

  1. Defina a rotina: dias, horários, se precisa dirigir, se fala português ou inglês com as crianças, se cozinha para elas.
  2. Defina o valor por hora: em Orlando, nanny costuma cobrar entre $20,79 e $26,36 por hora e babysitter entre $18,78 e $27,63 (Care.com, nov/2026). Veja quanto custa uma babá em Orlando.
  3. Publique a vaga: na Famyle é grátis e leva 1 minuto. As profissionais da região se candidatam e você recebe na hora o telefone e o WhatsApp de cada uma.
  4. Entreviste: pergunte sobre experiência com crianças da mesma idade, primeiros socorros (CPR), referências de famílias anteriores e disponibilidade.
  5. Faça um dia de teste pago antes de fechar.
  6. Combine por escrito: horário, tarefas, valor, hora extra, folgas e como encerrar o acordo.

O que muda em relação ao Brasil

  • Nos EUA o pagamento é por hora, não mensal. Hora extra e feriado se combinam antes.
  • Não existe carteira assinada nem FGTS. Mas, se a babá trabalha na sua rotina e você paga $3.000 ou mais no ano, você tem obrigações de imposto federal (o chamado nanny tax). Veja como contratar empregada doméstica na Flórida.
  • O salário mínimo da Flórida é $15,00 por hora desde 30/09/2026.

Publicar vaga de babá em Orlando (grátis)
faq: Quanto custa uma babá em Orlando por hora?
Nanny costuma cobrar entre $20,79 e $26,36 por hora e babysitter entre $18,78 e $27,63 por hora em Orlando (Care.com, novembro de 2026).
Preciso registrar a babá nos EUA?

Se ela trabalha na sua rotina e você paga $3.000 ou mais no ano de 2026, você deve recolher Social Security e Medicare (7,65% de cada lado) e declarar no Schedule H. A Flórida não tem imposto de renda estadual.
Dá para achar babá que fala português em Orlando?
Orlando tem uma comunidade brasileira grande, principalmente em Winter Garden, Windermere e Kissimmee. Ao publicar a vaga, informe que quer alguém que fale português.
guides_pt.answer: Para contratar babá em Orlando: defina a rotina e o valor por hora (nanny costuma cobrar de $20,79 a $26,36 por hora em 2026, segundo a Care.com), publique a vaga, entreviste, faça um dia de teste pago e combine tudo por escrito. Se pagar $3.000 ou mais no ano, há imposto federal a recolher (nanny tax).

guides_pt.title: Quanto custa uma babá em Orlando? Valores por hora e por mês (2026)
guides_pt.desc: Valor por hora de nanny e babysitter em Orlando, quanto fica por mês em tempo integral e quais impostos a família paga.
guides_pt.html:
Valores por hora em Orlando

QuemValor típicoFonte

Quanto fica por mês

Uma nanny em tempo integral, a $22 por hora e 40 horas por semana, custa cerca de $3.800 por mês antes dos impostos ($22 × 40 × 52 ÷ 12). Na faixa típica de Orlando, fica entre $3.600 e $4.600 por mês.

O que faz o valor subir ou descer

  • Número e idade das crianças: é comum somar $1 a $2 por hora por criança a mais.
  • Experiência, curso de primeiros socorros (CPR) e formação em educação infantil.
  • Dirigir: babá que leva e busca as crianças costuma cobrar mais.
  • Idiomas: babá bilíngue é muito procurada em Orlando.
  • Tempo integral ou eventual: em tempo integral, muitas famílias combinam um valor semanal.

Impostos que a família paga

Em 2026, se você paga $3.000 ou mais no ano para a babá, retém 7,65% do salário dela (Social Security e Medicare) e paga mais 7,65% do seu lado. Se pagar $1.000 ou mais num trimestre, entram também o imposto federal de desemprego (FUTA) e o reemployment tax da Flórida. Tudo é declarado no Schedule H, junto do seu imposto de renda. A Flórida não tem imposto de renda estadual.

Babá em Orlando ganha por hora ou por mês?
O mais comum é por hora. Em tempo integral, muitas famílias combinam um valor semanal com base nas horas.
Preciso pagar hora extra para a babá?
Pela lei federal (FLSA), funcionária doméstica que não mora na sua casa tem direito a hora extra acima de 40 horas por semana. Combine isso por escrito antes de começar.

Diarista autônoma ou empresa de limpeza?

  • Diarista autônoma: costuma sair mais barato e é sempre a mesma pessoa.
  • Empresa de limpeza: cuida do seguro e manda substituta se alguém faltar, mas cobra a margem dela e pode mandar pessoas diferentes.

A diarista é minha funcionária?

Precisa dar gorjeta para a diarista?
Para diarista fixa contratada direto, gorjeta não é obrigatória. Muitas famílias dão um bônus de fim de ano no valor de uma faxina.
É melhor diarista ou empresa de limpeza?
Diarista autônoma costuma sair mais barato e é sempre a mesma pessoa. Empresa garante substituta e seguro, mas cobra mais.
guides_pt.answer: Uma faxina em Orlando custa de $20,25 a $25,07 por hora em 2026 (Care.com, novembro de 2026). A faxina comum de uma casa de 3 quartos leva de 3 a 4 horas, ou seja, de $70 a $90 por visita. Diarista autônoma costuma sair mais barato que empresa de limpeza.

guides_pt.title: Como contratar empregada doméstica na Flórida legalmente (2026)
guides_pt.desc: O que a família precisa saber para contratar babá, housekeeper ou cozinheira na Flórida: salário mínimo, nanny tax, reemployment tax, Form I-9 e contrato.
guides_pt.html:
Para quem vem do Brasil, a lógica é diferente: não há carteira assinada nem FGTS, mas há impostos que a família recolhe quando a profissional é sua funcionária. Este guia resume o essencial. Não é orientação jurídica nem tributária: em caso de dúvida, fale com um contador americano.

1. Ela é sua funcionária?

Se você define o que é feito e como, a profissional em geral é sua funcionária doméstica (household employee): é o caso da babá ou da housekeeper no seu horário. Se ela tem o próprio negócio, leva o material e atende o público, em geral é autônoma (IRS Publicação 926).

2. Pague ao menos o salário mínimo

O salário mínimo da Flórida é $15,00 por hora desde 30/09/2026 e será corrigido pela inflação todo ano a partir de 2027.

3. Impostos federais (o nanny tax)

  • Social Security e Medicare: se você paga $3.000 ou mais no ano de 2026 a uma funcionária doméstica, retém 6,2% + 1,45% do salário dela e paga o mesmo valor do seu lado.
  • FUTA: se você paga $1.000 ou mais num trimestre, deve o imposto federal de desemprego.
  • Tudo vai no Schedule H, junto do seu Form 1040, e você entrega à funcionária o Form W-2.

4. Impostos da Flórida

  • Não há imposto de renda estadual para reter.
  • Reemployment tax: vale se você paga $1.000 ou mais num trimestre por serviço doméstico; incide sobre os primeiros $7.000 por funcionária no ano, a 2,7% para novos empregadores (Florida Department of Revenue).

5. Autorização de trabalho (Form I-9)

Quem contrata funcionária doméstica deve preencher o Form I-9, que confirma a identidade e a autorização para trabalhar nos EUA. Trabalho esporádico e irregular, como uma babysitter de vez em quando, fica de fora. Fonte: USCIS, I-9 Central.

6. Combine por escrito

Horário, tarefas, valor por hora, hora extra, folgas e como qualquer um dos dois encerra o acordo.

Fontes: IRS Publicação 926 (2026) · Florida Department of Revenue · USCIS · Constituição da Flórida, art. X §24.
faq: Qual o limite do nanny tax em 2026?
$3.000 pagos em dinheiro a uma funcionária doméstica no ano (IRS Publicação 926).
Preciso reter imposto de renda estadual na Flórida?
Não. A Flórida não tem imposto de renda estadual.
Existe FGTS ou carteira assinada nos EUA?
Não. As obrigações da família são os impostos federais (Social Security, Medicare e FUTA), o reemployment tax da Flórida quando passa do limite, o Form W-2 e o Form I-9.
guides_pt.answer: Para contratar empregada doméstica na Flórida em 2026: pague ao menos o mínimo de $15,00 por hora; se pagar $3.000 ou mais no ano, recolha Social Security e Medicare (7,65% de cada lado) e declare no Schedule H; preencha o Form I-9. Não há carteira assinada, FGTS nem imposto de renda estadual.

guides_pt.title: Babá e diarista em Winter Garden e Horizon West: guia para famílias brasileiras
guides_pt.desc: Como encontrar babá, diarista ou housekeeper em Winter Garden, Horizon West e Windermere, onde mora boa parte da comunidade brasileira de Orlando.
guides_pt.html:
Winter Garden, Horizon West (CEP 34787) e Windermere concentram muitas famílias brasileiras em Orlando. É também onde a Famyle começou nos EUA.

Fonte: Care.com, Orlando, novembro de 2026.

Dicas para quem acabou de chegar

  • Peça referências de outras famílias e faça um dia de teste pago.
  • Se as crianças ainda estão aprendendo inglês, uma babá que fale português ajuda na adaptação.
  • Combine tudo por escrito: horário, valor por hora e hora extra.
  • Se a profissional for sua funcionária, veja as regras da Flórida.

Como a Famyle funciona

Você publica a vaga de graça. As profissionais da região se candidatam, você recebe na hora o telefone e o WhatsApp de cada uma e contrata direto, sem intermediário. Nada do seu contato aparece na vaga. As 100 primeiras famílias de Orlando ganham 12 meses grátis quando a Famyle começar a cobrar.

faq: Tem babá brasileira em Winter Garden?
A região tem uma comunidade brasileira grande. Ao publicar a vaga, diga que prefere alguém que fale português.

Os valores seguem os de Orlando: faxina entre $20,25 e $25,07 por hora (Care.com, novembro de 2026).
A Famyle cobra da família?
Não. Publicar a vaga e falar com as profissionais é grátis. As 100 primeiras famílias de Orlando ganham 12 meses grátis quando a Famyle começar a cobrar.
guides_pt.answer: Em Winter Garden e Horizon West, babá (nanny) custa de $20,79 a $26,36 por hora e faxina de $20,25 a $25,07 por hora em 2026 (Care.com, Orlando, novembro de 2026). A região tem uma comunidade brasileira grande: ao publicar a vaga na Famyle, que é grátis, diga se prefere alguém que fale português.
